# Shipwreck & Sail — Visual Inspiration Board
**Purpose:** Coordinate the shared visual vision across team members and coding agents.  
**How to use:** Replace each `📌 [IMAGE SLOT]` block with a reference image. Add a one-line note beneath each image describing what specifically to take from it (colour, shape language, texture, mood, etc.).

---

## 1. Overall Aesthetic Direction

The game targets a **low-poly voxel** art style — chunky geometry, flat or lightly textured surfaces, warm maritime palette. References here set the tone for *everything* else.

| Slot | What to find |
|------|-------------|
| 1-A | Voxel / low-poly game with strong sea / nautical theme |
| 1-B | Colour palette reference — warm wood tones, ocean blues, rope yellows |
| 1-C | Lighting mood — midday sun on water, overcast storm lighting |
| 1-D | Overall HUD aesthetic — clean, parchment-y, slightly worn |

## 2. Ship Classes

Three ship classes escalate in size across seven days. References here define the silhouette and voxel resolution for each. All ships are built on a voxel grid — the reference images should inform proportions and landmark features, not photorealistic detail.

| Ship | Grid Size | Days |
|------|----------|------|
| Sloop | 24 × 10 × 6 | 1–2 |
| Brigantine | 40 × 14 × 8 | 3–5 |
| Galleon | 64 × 18 × 10 | 6–7 |

---

## 7. Colour & Lighting Direction Summary

Once all slots above are filled in, use this section to distil the agreed-upon direction into actionable targets for the Three.js lighting setup.

| Element | Agreed Direction | Three.js Implementation Note |
|---------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| Ambient light colour | | `THREE.AmbientLight( colour, intensity )` |
| Directional / sun light | | `THREE.DirectionalLight` — angle, colour |
| Ocean shader base colour | | `uWaterColor` uniform |
| Ocean shader highlight | | `uFoamColor` uniform |
| Storm darkening factor | | Lerp ambient intensity toward dark value |
| Voxel wood material | | `MeshLambertMaterial` or `MeshToonMaterial` |
| Damaged cell tint | | Overlay colour on `DAMAGED` state material |
| Flooded cell tint | | Translucent blue, `MeshPhongMaterial` with opacity |
